# FlexVara

> A single-page buyer's guide to FlexVara, the NUVICA Wellness joint wellness capsule, sold as 60 capsules per bottle and taken two capsules daily with water. Written for readers in the United States at https://flexvara-co.vercel.app/. Orders complete on the official checkout with ClickBank as retailer of record. Last reviewed 16 November 2026.

FlexVara publishes all seven of its ingredient amounts rather than grouping them into a blend total. One two-capsule serving provides NEM eggshell membrane 500 mg, boswellia extract 150 mg, calcium 75 mg at 6% of the Daily Value, turmeric root extract 50 mg standardised to 95% curcuminoids, ginger root extract 20 mg, hydrolyzed collagen 5 mg and black pepper fruit extract 5 mg, totalling 805 mg of active material. Carrier ingredients are microcrystalline cellulose, hypromellose for the capsule shell, magnesium stearate and silicon dioxide. The label carries a CONTAINS EGG allergen declaration because the lead ingredient is derived from hen eggshells; the product is otherwise stated free of dairy, soy and gluten and described as non-GMO. A bottle lasts 30 days and NUVICA recommends three to six months of use. Three packages are sold: two bottles at $69 each ($138 plus $9.95 postage, about $2.47 a day with postage included), three bottles at $59 each ($177 posted free, about $1.97 a day) and six bottles at $49 each ($294 posted free, about $1.63 a day). The newsletter bonus and free postage attach to the three and six bottle packages. Every package carries a 90-day money-back guarantee. One payment, no subscription. Sold to adults 18 and over.

## Sources cited on this page

- [NIAMS: osteoarthritis research and resources](https://www.niams.nih.gov/health-topics/osteoarthritis/more-info): the US institute for arthritis and musculoskeletal conditions, with plain-language resources.
- [MedlinePlus: osteoarthritis](https://medlineplus.gov/osteoarthritis.html): consumer background on joint conditions and how to prepare for a clinical appointment.
- [NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: calcium](https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Calcium/): recommended intakes and upper limits, relevant to the 75 mg in each serving.
- [NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: what you need to know](https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/WYNTK-Consumer/): a plain-language primer on what dietary supplements are and how they are regulated.
- [NIH LiverTox: turmeric](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK548561/): background on turmeric, including rare liver-injury reports that chiefly involve high-dose curcumin products.
- [FDA: dietary supplements](https://www.fda.gov/food/dietary-supplements): supplements fall under food law rather than medicines law in the United States.
- [FTC: health claims](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/advertising-marketing/health-claims): the advertising rules a supplement health claim must meet.
